questions.question: In which athletics event did Eldhose Paul win a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2022?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Triple Jump**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eldhose Paul** created history by winning the **gold medal** in the **Triple Jump** event at the **Commonwealth Games 2022**.
 
• This victory marked India's **first-ever gold medal** in the **Triple Jump** at the Commonwealth Games.
 
• Eldhose Paul recorded a jump of **17.03 meters**, securing his top spot.
 
• The event took place at the **Alexander Stadium** in Birmingham, England.
 
• He was followed by his compatriot **Abdulla Aboobacker Narangolintevid**, who won the **silver medal**, making it a historic **1-2 finish for India** in the event.
 
• The **Triple Jump** is an athletic event that involves three phases of jumping: the **hop, step, and jump**.
 
• Eldhose Paul's achievement is seen as a significant milestone in **Indian athletics**, showcasing the country's growing prowess in field events.
 
• He hails from **Kerala, India**, and has been actively contributing to India’s success in international athletics competitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Javelin Throw**__

 __
 
• The **Javelin Throw** is a track and field event where athletes throw a spear-like implement called a **javelin**.
 
• India's **Neeraj Chopra** won the **gold medal** in Javelin Throw at the **Tokyo Olympics 2020**, bringing global attention to the event in India.
 
 
 
• **Shot Put**__
 __
 
• The **Shot Put** involves throwing a heavy spherical object, called a **shot**, as far as possible.
 
• It is one of the oldest events in athletics and requires significant **strength and technique**.
 
 
 
• **Long Jump**__
 
 
• The **Long Jump** is an event where athletes sprint and jump as far as possible from a take-off point.
 
• It is measured based on the **distance covered** from the take-off board to the nearest mark in the landing area.

questions.question: The Swaraj party was formed within ________ with the thought of contesting elections to enter the legislative councils with a view to obstructing the governance of the colonial government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Congress**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swaraj Party** was formed in 1923 by prominent leaders **Motilal Nehru** and **Chittaranjan Das**, who were members of the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• The party emerged as a result of dissatisfaction within the Congress regarding the **Non-Cooperation Movement**, which had been suspended by Mahatma Gandhi after the **Chauri Chaura incident**.
 
• Its primary goal was to contest elections to enter the **legislative councils** and use the councils as platforms to oppose and obstruct the policies of the **colonial government**.
 
• The Swaraj Party aimed to achieve **self-rule** or "Swaraj" for India by adopting a more confrontational approach within the legislative framework.
 
• They believed that using the councils would allow them to expose the weaknesses of the **British administration** and advocate for Indian interests.
 
• The Swaraj Party operated within the **Indian National Congress** but maintained its distinct identity and objectives.
 
• Leaders of the Swaraj Party focused on issues like **civil liberties, repeal of repressive laws, and reduction of heavy taxation**, which directly impacted the Indian population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Unionist Party**__

 __
 
• The Unionist Party was a **political party** active in the **Punjab region** during British India formed in **1923**.
 
• It primarily represented the interests of landlords and agricultural communities in Punjab.
 
• This party was not directly associated with the **Indian National Congress** or the Swaraj movement.
 
• The Unionist Party played a significant role in regional politics rather than national independence efforts.
 
 
 
• **Independent Labour Party**__
 __
 
• The Independent Labour Party was founded by **B. R. Ambedkar** in 1936.
 
• Its focus was on addressing issues faced by the **Dalits** and other marginalized communities in India.
 
• It was not involved in the Swaraj movement or legislative council obstruction as its primary agenda was social justice and labor rights.
 
 
 
• **All India Muslim League**__
 
 
• The All India Muslim League was established in 1906 to safeguard the political rights of **Muslims in India**.
 
• It later played a prominent role in advocating for the creation of **Pakistan**.
 
• The Muslim League was not involved in the Swaraj Party's objectives, as its focus was more on communal and Muslim representation rather than legislative obstruction of British governance.

questions.question: How does salt contribute to the preservation of food?

options.text: By inhibiting the growth of microorganisms through osmosis.
By reducing the pH of the food.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**By inhibiting the growth of microorganisms through osmosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Salt** plays a critical role in food preservation by creating an environment where microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, and yeast cannot thrive.
 
• The process is known as **osmosis**, where salt draws water out of microbial cells, leading to **dehydration** and the inhibition of their growth.
 
• Microorganisms need water to survive and reproduce. By reducing the **water activity** in food, salt effectively prevents spoilage.
 
• Salt also enhances the shelf life of food items, making it a widely used method for preserving foods like **meats, fish, pickles, and vegetables.**
 
• In addition to preserving food, salt contributes to improving the **taste and texture** of preserved items.
 
• Historically, salt has been used in preservation for thousands of years, especially before the invention of refrigeration. Examples include salted meats and fish, such as **beef jerky and salted cod.**
 
• Modern industries still utilize salt preservation, especially in the production of cured foods like **sausages, ham, and pickled products.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **By acting as an antioxidant**__

 __
 
• Antioxidants are substances that prevent oxidation, a chemical reaction that can cause food spoilage and rancidity.
 
• However, salt is not an antioxidant. Antioxidants include substances like **Vitamin C, Vitamin E, and compounds such as BHT or BHA.**
 
 
 
• **By reducing the pH of the food**__
 __
 
• Reducing pH means making the food more acidic, which can inhibit microbial growth.
 
• Acidification is a common preservation method but is achieved through substances like **vinegar or citric acid**, not salt.
 
 
 
• **By promoting the Maillard reaction**__
 
 
• The Maillard reaction is a chemical process that occurs between amino acids and reducing sugars under heat, responsible for browning and flavor development in cooked foods.
 
• Salt does not promote the Maillard reaction directly; this reaction is influenced by factors such as **temperature and the presence of sugars and proteins.**

questions.question: Which of the following Census decades in India recorded the highest crude death rate?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1911-1921**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The decade **1911-1921** recorded the **highest crude death rate** in India.
 
• This was primarily due to the **1918 influenza pandemic**, commonly known as the **Spanish Flu**, which caused a significant loss of life.
 
• The pandemic is estimated to have killed around **12-17 million people in India**, which was about 5% of the population at the time.
 
• Other contributing factors included **poor health infrastructure**, lack of access to modern medicine, and widespread **poverty** during this period.
 
• The decade also saw a **decline in population growth** due to the high mortality rate caused by the pandemic and other diseases.
 
• The **British colonial administration** was unable to effectively handle the health crisis, further exacerbating the situation.
 
• This period is often studied in the context of its **public health challenges** and demographic impact on colonial India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1911-1921: Correct Answer**__

 __
 
• The **1918 influenza pandemic** was a global catastrophe, but its impact on India was disproportionately large due to pre-existing vulnerabilities like **malnutrition** and **overcrowding**.
 
• This event is considered one of the most devastating pandemics in human history, with India bearing a significant part of the global death toll.
 
 
 
• **1941-1951**__
 __
 
• This decade saw improvements in public health due to **post-World War II advancements** and the introduction of modern medical practices.
 
• India also experienced the effects of the **Partition**, which led to mass migrations, but health indicators like the crude death rate were relatively better compared to earlier decades.
 
 
 
• **1931-1941**__
 __
 
• This period witnessed gradual improvements in public health infrastructure, but infectious diseases like **malaria** and **tuberculosis** were still prevalent.
 
• The crude death rate was high but did not surpass the 1911-1921 period.
 
 
 
• **1991-2001**__
 
 
• By this time, India's health indicators had improved significantly due to **advancements in healthcare**, better access to medicines, and **government health programs**.
 
• The crude death rate was at one of its lowest historical levels during this period.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles is automatically suspended when an emergency is declared on the grounds of external aggression?

• During a **National Emergency** declared on the grounds of **external aggression** or war, the rights guaranteed under Article 19 are automatically suspended to ensure **national security**.
 
• The suspension of Article 19 allows the government to impose **necessary restrictions** on freedoms to address the emergency effectively.
 
• This automatic suspension aligns with the need to balance **individual rights** with the **security and sovereignty** of the nation during critical situations.
 
• Article 19 is a part of the **Fundamental Rights** under Part III of the Indian Constitution, which are subject to certain restrictions during emergencies.
 
• The emergency provision is governed by **Article 352** of the Constitution, which provides the framework for declaring a National Emergency.
 
• Historically, Article 19 was suspended during significant emergencies such as the **Indo-China War (1962)**, the **Indo-Pakistan War (1971)**, and the **National Emergency (1975-77)**.

• Unlike Article 19, Article 32 is not automatically suspended during emergencies; however, its application may be restricted in certain cases.

• During emergencies, preventive detention laws may override the protections under Article 22.

questions.question: Select the correct sentence about the water table.

options.text: The lower level of the groundwater layer is called water table.
Water cannot be found below the water table.
The water table varies from place to place.
The water table cannot be changed at a given place.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The water table varies from place to place**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **water table** refers to the upper surface of the groundwater layer where the soil and rocks are saturated with water.
 
• The depth of the water table is not uniform; it **varies from one location to another** depending on factors such as **geographical conditions, rainfall, and human activities**.
 
• It can be deeper in areas with **arid climates** due to lower precipitation levels and shallower in regions with **high rainfall or near water bodies.**
 
• The water table can also fluctuate over time at a given place due to **seasonal changes**, such as increased groundwater recharge during monsoons.
 
• Human activities like **excessive extraction of groundwater for agriculture, industry, or domestic use** can lead to a decline in the water table, while conservation efforts can help replenish it.
 
• Understanding variations in the water table is crucial for sustainable groundwater management and planning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The lower level of the groundwater layer is called water table.**__

 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because the water table represents the **upper surface of the groundwater layer**, not the lower level.
 
• The lower levels of the groundwater layer are referred to as **aquitards or confined aquifers**, depending on the geological structure.
 
 
 
• **Water cannot be found below the water table.**__
 __
 
• This statement is false because water can exist below the water table in deeper layers called **aquifers.**
 
• These aquifers are often tapped through **borewells** or **deep wells** for water extraction.
 
 
 
• **The water table cannot be changed at a given place.**__
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because the water table can change due to factors like **seasonal variations** in rainfall, groundwater extraction, and recharge processes.
 
• Over-extraction and urbanization can lead to a significant decline in the **water table level** over time.

questions.question: Brahmo Samaj, the theistic movement within Hinduism, was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1828**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brahmo Samaj** was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in the year **1828**.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was a **reformist and theistic movement** within Hinduism, aiming to bring about **social, political, and religious changes**.
 
• It promoted the belief in a **formless, eternal, and omnipresent God** and rejected idol worship and meaningless rituals.
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, often regarded as the **Father of the Indian Renaissance**, was instrumental in initiating this reform movement to modernize Hindu society.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj played a significant role in the abolition of **social evils like Sati**, child marriage, and caste discrimination.
 
• It emphasized the importance of **education**, particularly for women, and encouraged **scientific inquiry** and rational thinking.
 
• The movement also advocated for **monotheism**, equality, and the elimination of superstitions in Indian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1839**__

 __
 
• This year does not relate to the foundation of the Brahmo Samaj. However, it was a period marked by significant reformist activities in India.
 
 
 
• **1856**__
 __
 
• In this year, the **Widow Remarriage Act** was passed under the guidance of **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**, another prominent social reformer.
 
 
 
• **1879**__
 
 
• No significant event related to the Brahmo Samaj occurred in this year. However, by this time, the Brahmo Samaj had split into two factions: **Adi Brahmo Samaj** and **Sadharan Brahmo Samaj**.

questions.question: If the body of an animal can be divided into two indistinguishable left and right halves through only one plane, then it possesses:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**bilateral symmetry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bilateral symmetry** refers to a body structure where an organism can be divided into two identical halves along a single plane.
 
• It is a common feature observed in animals belonging to the **phylum Chordata**, which includes mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes.
 
• This type of symmetry facilitates **directional movement**, as organisms with bilateral symmetry tend to have a distinct head (anterior) and tail (posterior) region.
 
• Examples of organisms with bilateral symmetry include **humans, dogs, cats, insects, and birds**.
 
• Bilateral symmetry is crucial for the development of complex body structures, including **sensory organs** and the **central nervous system**.
 
• This symmetry type is advantageous for the evolution of organisms that exhibit active locomotion and show specialization in body regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Centre of symmetry**__

 __
 
• This term is not applicable to biological classifications. It is more commonly used in **geometry and crystallography** to describe a point in a figure or structure where symmetrical elements converge.
 
 
 
• **Asymmetricity**__
 __
 
• Asymmetricity refers to the absence of any symmetry in an organism. Examples include **sponges (Porifera)**, which do not exhibit a defined body plan or symmetry.
 
• Such organisms often rely on a simple structure for functions like feeding and reproduction.
 
 
 
• **Radial symmetry**__
 
 
• Radial symmetry is observed in organisms whose body parts are arranged around a central axis, allowing multiple planes to divide the body into identical halves.
 
• Examples include **cnidarians (jellyfish, corals)** and **echinoderms (starfish, sea urchins)**.
 
• This type of symmetry is well-suited for animals that interact with the environment equally in all directions.

questions.question: Which volume of the 'Akbar-Nama' is known as Ain-i-Akbari and deals with Akbar's administration, household, army and revenues and geography of his empire?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Third**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Akbar-Nama** is a historical account written by **Abu'l-Fazl**, one of the Navratnas of Emperor Akbar's court.
 
• It consists of three volumes, of which the **third volume** is known as the **Ain-i-Akbari**.
 
• The Ain-i-Akbari is an administrative document that provides detailed information about **Akbar's governance**, including his **administration, household, army, revenue system, and the geography of his empire**.
 
• This volume is divided into five books, each covering distinct aspects of Akbar's reign:
 
 
• **Book One:** Deals with the imperial household and administration.
 
• **Book Two:** Discusses the army, weapons, and military organization.
 
• **Book Three:** Covers Akbar's revenue system and land measurements.
 
• **Book Four:** Includes information about the culture, arts, and sciences.
 
• **Book Five:** Contains a biography of the author and miscellaneous topics.
 
 
 
• The Ain-i-Akbari is regarded as a remarkable source of information about the functioning of the **Mughal Empire** under Akbar's rule.
 
• The text reflects Akbar's policies of cultural integration, administrative efficiency, and his interest in compiling detailed information about his empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Second Volume**__

 __
 
• The second volume of the Akbar-Nama provides a detailed account of Akbar's reign, including his wars, campaigns, and administrative reforms.
 
• It primarily focuses on the historical narrative of the events during Akbar's rule.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Volume**__
 __
 
• There is no fourth volume in the Akbar-Nama, as it consists of only three volumes. This option is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Volume**__
 
 
• Similar to the fourth volume, the Akbar-Nama does not have a fifth volume. Hence, this option is invalid.

questions.question: Kelucharan Mohapatra is associated with which of the following dances?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra** was a legendary Indian classical dancer and Guru of **Odissi**, one of the eight classical dance forms of India.
 
• He is credited with reviving the **Odissi dance**, which originated in the state of **Odisha**.
 
• His contribution was significant in shaping and popularizing Odissi as a structured and prominent classical dance form on national and international stages.
 
• Kelucharan Mohapatra’s performances were known for their **grace**, **expressive gestures**, and **technical precision**.
 
• He was also instrumental in choreographing many Odissi dance pieces, integrating the **mythological themes** and **spiritual essence** of Odisha.
 
• He received several prestigious honors, including the **Padma Vibhushan**, **Padma Bhushan**, and **Padma Shri**, for his immense contributions to Indian art and culture.
 
• Kelucharan Mohapatra also trained numerous disciples who went on to become renowned Odissi dancers, ensuring the legacy of this art form continues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fugdi**__

 __
 
• **Fugdi** is a traditional folk dance of the Indian state of **Goa**.
 
• It is performed by women in groups during festivals and religious occasions, particularly during the **Ganesh Chaturthi festival**.
 
• The dance is accompanied by rhythmic clapping and distinctive breathing sounds made by the performers.
 
 
 
• **Dumhal**__
 __
 
• **Dumhal** is a traditional folk dance performed by the **Watal tribe** of **Jammu and Kashmir**.
 
• It is usually performed by men wearing long, colorful robes and conical caps, often during **special ceremonies** or celebrations.
 
• The performers carry a banner, and the dance involves intricate movements and singing.
 
 
 
• **Bihu**__
 
 
• **Bihu** is a folk dance from the Indian state of **Assam**.
 
• It is performed during the **Bihu festival**, which marks the Assamese New Year and the harvest season.
 
• The dance is characterized by its **energetic movements** and vibrant costumes.
 
• It is accompanied by traditional Assamese musical instruments like the **dhol** and **pepa**.

questions.question: Before the introduction of Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), what type of surveys did the National Statistical Office (NSO) conduct for employment and unemployment indicators in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Quinquennial surveys**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Before the introduction of the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**, the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** conducted **Quinquennial surveys** to collect data on **employment and unemployment indicators** in India.
 
• **Quinquennial** refers to a survey conducted once every **five years**.
 
• The **Employment-Unemployment Surveys** (EUS) conducted by NSO were part of its **National Sample Survey (NSS)** rounds.
 
• The quinquennial surveys provided detailed information on various aspects of employment, such as **worker participation rates, unemployment rates, types of employment** (self-employed, regular, casual labor), and **sectoral distribution**.
 
• These surveys were instrumental in understanding the **labor market dynamics** in India before the PLFS replaced them as a more frequent and comprehensive survey mechanism.
 
• The **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**, introduced by NSO in **2017**, now provides annual and quarterly estimates to better reflect changes in employment and unemployment trends.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biennial surveys**__

 __
 
• **Biennial** means surveys conducted once every **two years**.
 
• While biennial surveys are common in many sectors, the NSO did not use this frequency for employment and unemployment surveys before PLFS.
 
 
 
• **Decennial surveys**__
 __
 
• **Decennial** refers to surveys conducted once every **ten years**.
 
• Decennial surveys are typically used for large-scale data collection efforts like the **Census of India**, but they are not used for employment and unemployment surveys due to the need for more frequent data updates.
 
 
 
• **Monthly surveys**__
 
 
• While **monthly surveys** are used in some countries for employment statistics, the NSO did not conduct monthly surveys for employment and unemployment data prior to the introduction of PLFS.
 
• Monthly frequency is often used for high-frequency indicators like **inflation** or **industrial production.**

questions.question: Under Article 165, the Governor appoints a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court to be the ________ for the State.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Advocate-General**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 165** of the Constitution of India, the **Governor** appoints the **Advocate-General** for the state.
 
• The Advocate-General must be qualified to be appointed as a **Judge of a High Court**.
 
• This means the person must have been an advocate for at least **10 years** or a judicial officer for at least **10 years**.
 
• The Advocate-General is the highest law officer in the state and advises the **state government** on legal matters.
 
• The Advocate-General has the right to participate in the proceedings of the state legislature and express views, but they do not have the right to vote.
 
• The position is analogous to the **Attorney General of India** at the central level.
 
• The Advocate-General performs duties such as defending the state in legal cases and representing the state in legal matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chief Minister**__

 __
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the elected head of the government in a state and is not appointed by the Governor under Article 165.
 
• The Chief Minister is chosen by the majority party or coalition in the state legislature.
 
• He/she acts as the chief executive of the state, overseeing the administration and implementing policies.
 
 
 
• **Attorney General**__
 __
 
• The **Attorney General** is the highest law officer in the country and is appointed by the President of India under **Article 76**.
 
• The Attorney General advises the central government on legal matters and represents the government in cases before the Supreme Court.
 
• This position is not related to Article 165, which deals with states.
 
 
 
• **Comptroller Auditor General (CAG)**__
 
 
• The **Comptroller Auditor General** is appointed by the President of India under **Article 148**.
 
• The CAG is responsible for auditing government expenditures and ensuring accountability in financial matters.
 
• This position is unrelated to Article 165 or legal advice to state governments.

questions.question: Who among the following was a contemporary of Buddha, but is not considered the first founder of the religion?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mahavira Swami**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahavira Swami** was a contemporary of **Gautama Buddha**.
 
• He is regarded as the **24th Tirthankara** of Jainism but not the founder of the religion.
 
• Jainism is believed to have originated much earlier, with **Rishabhanath** as the first Tirthankara.
 
• **Mahavira Swami** propagated Jainism during the 6th century BCE.
 
• He emphasized principles such as **Ahimsa (non-violence), Aparigraha (non-possession), and Satya (truth).**
 
• Mahavira advocated a life of austerity and self-discipline, focusing on spiritual liberation or **Moksha.**
 
• He attained **Kevala Jnana** (omniscience) and spent the rest of his life spreading Jain teachings.
 
• Mahavira Swami's teachings laid the foundation for the organized Jain community, but Jainism itself predates him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rishabhanath**__

 __
 
• **Rishabhanath** is considered the **first Tirthankara** of Jainism.
 
• He is believed to have lived millions of years ago, according to Jain texts.
 
• Rishabhanath is associated with the beginning of human civilization, including the introduction of agriculture and societal norms.
 
 
 
• **Bhadrabahu**__
 __
 
• **Bhadrabahu** was a prominent Jain monk and spiritual leader.
 
• He is known for his association with **Chandragupta Maurya**, the founder of the Maurya Empire.
 
• Bhadrabahu was instrumental in preserving Jain teachings and scriptures during his time.
 
 
 
• **Arishtanemi**__
 
 
• **Arishtanemi**, also known as **Neminatha**, was the **22nd Tirthankara** of Jainism.
 
• He is said to have been a cousin of **Lord Krishna**, highlighting a connection between Jain and Hindu traditions.
 
• Arishtanemi is associated with the teachings of renunciation and spiritual discipline.

questions.question: The shotgun (in the shooting sport) is a _______ gauge having a calibre of 18.5-millimetres (The gauge is a unit of measurement for firearms).
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**12 gauge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **12-gauge shotgun** is one of the most common types of shotguns used in sporting events, hunting, and law enforcement worldwide.
 
• The term **"gauge"** refers to the internal diameter of the barrel and is determined by the number of lead balls the size of the barrel bore that it takes to weigh one pound.
 
• For a **12-gauge shotgun**, this means that 12 lead balls of the barrel's diameter equal one pound in weight.
 
• The **calibre** of a 12-gauge shotgun is approximately **18.5 millimetres**, making it suitable for a wide variety of uses including clay target shooting and bird hunting.
 
• Shotguns with a **12-gauge** configuration are known for their versatility, offering a balance between power and recoil, which makes them a preferred choice for many users.
 
• This gauge provides a larger spread of pellets or shot, increasing the likelihood of hitting a moving target, particularly in sports like skeet and trap shooting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **10-gauge**__

 __
 
• A **10-gauge shotgun** has a larger bore diameter than a 12-gauge, making it more powerful but with increased recoil.
 
• It is typically used in applications requiring more power, such as hunting larger game or waterfowl.
 
• Due to its higher recoil, it is less commonly used compared to the versatile 12-gauge.
 
 
 
• **Understanding "gauge" as a term**__
 __
 
• The **gauge** system originated in England and is based on the number of lead balls of the barrel’s diameter that add up to one pound.
 
• For example, a 12-gauge indicates that 12 lead balls of the bore's diameter weigh one pound, while a 10-gauge would mean 10 lead balls.
 
 
 
• **Applications of 12-gauge shotguns**__
 
 
• Widely used in sporting events like **skeet shooting**, **trap shooting**, and **hunting**.
 
• It is also popular in **self-defense** and law enforcement due to its reliability and effectiveness.

questions.question: Which day is celebrated as International Day of Non-Violence?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**2nd October**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Day of Non-Violence** is celebrated every year on **2nd October**, the birth anniversary of **Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, also known as the "Father of the Nation" in India, was a global symbol of **non-violence and peace.**
 
• The day was established by the **United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)** on **15 June 2007**, through a resolution.
 
• It aims to spread the message of **non-violence** through education and public awareness.
 
• Gandhi's philosophy of **Ahimsa** (non-violence) was pivotal in India's struggle for independence against British colonial rule.
 
• His teachings have inspired civil rights movements and leaders globally, such as **Martin Luther King Jr.** and **Nelson Mandela**.
 
• The day serves as a reminder to resolve conflicts and disputes through **dialogue** and **peaceful means**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **31st October**__

 __
 
• **31st October** is observed as **National Unity Day** or **Rashtriya Ekta Diwas** in India.
 
• This day marks the birth anniversary of **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, known as the "**Iron Man of India**."
 
• It is celebrated to recognize Patel's role in the **unification of India** post-independence.
 
 
 
• **31st January**__
 __
 
• **31st January** does not have a significant international or national observance related to the theme of non-violence.
 
• It is typically a regular day without any globally recognized events.
 
 
 
• **15th August**__
 
 
• **15th August** is celebrated as **Independence Day** in India.
 
• This day commemorates India's independence from **British colonial rule** on **15th August 1947**.
 
• It is observed with flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, and cultural events across the country.

questions.question: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 4 August 2023, which repeals the _____________________________.

options.text: Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2007
Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008
Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2009
Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2006

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Anusandhan National Research Foundation (NRF) Bill, 2023** was introduced in the Lok Sabha on **4 August 2023**. It aims to enhance and promote research and innovation in India.
 
• This bill seeks to repeal the **Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008** and subsume the **Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB)** into the NRF.
 
• The SERB was established in **2008** as a statutory body to promote basic research in science and engineering.
 
• The **Anusandhan NRF** is designed to focus on fostering innovation, enhancing research capacities, and promoting a collaborative ecosystem among academia, industries, and research institutions.
 
• The NRF will ensure better coordination among various research organizations and will provide funding for **high-quality research** across disciplines.
 
• It also aims to encourage **private sector participation** in research and innovation.
 
• The establishment of NRF is part of the government's vision under the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020** to strengthen the research ecosystem in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2007**__

 __
 
• The **Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2007** is not a valid act. The SERB was established under the **Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008**, making the 2007 option irrelevant in this context.
 
 
 
• **Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2009**__
 __
 
• The **Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB)** was not established in 2009. It was created under the **Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008**, which came into effect in **2008**.
 
 
 
• **Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2006**__
 
 
• There is no record of a **Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2006**. The SERB was officially established under the **2008 Act**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main objective of the DWCRA model of SHGs?

options.text: To provide education opportunities for rural children
To provide housing support for rural families
To provide self-employment opportunities for rural women
To provide healthcare services to rural women

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**To provide self-employment opportunities for rural women**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DWCRA** stands for **Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas**.
 
• The model was introduced under the **Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP)** in **1982**.
 
• The primary focus of DWCRA is to empower **rural women** by providing them with opportunities for **self-employment**.
 
• It aims to improve the **socio-economic status** of women by enabling them to participate in income-generating activities.
 
• The model encourages the formation of **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**, which are small groups of women who pool resources and work collectively.
 
• These SHGs are provided with **financial support**, training, and technical guidance to start small enterprises such as handicrafts, tailoring, animal husbandry, and farming.
 
• DWCRA also promotes the creation of **cooperative societies** to market the products made by rural women, ensuring fair prices and sustained income.
 
• This initiative not only boosts the **financial independence** of women but also improves their **decision-making power** in households and communities.
 
• By encouraging self-employment, DWCRA contributes to **poverty alleviation** and fosters **gender equality** in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: To provide education opportunities for rural children**__

 __
 
• Although education in rural areas is important, it is not the primary focus of the **DWCRA model**.
 
• Education-related programs are generally implemented under other schemes such as the **Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan**.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: To provide housing support for rural families**__
 __
 
• Housing support in rural areas is addressed by schemes like the **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**.
 
• DWCRA primarily focuses on **empowering rural women**, not providing housing solutions.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To provide healthcare services to rural women**__
 
 
• Healthcare services for rural women are offered under programs such as **Janani Suraksha Yojana** and **National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)**.
 
• While DWCRA indirectly contributes to better health by improving women's financial independence, healthcare is not its core objective.
